summary.text: A king tide is an exceptionally high spring tide, usually one that comes when the Moon is closest to Earth around the time Earth is closest to the Sun.
Spring tides come at new and full moon, when the Moon's and Sun's pulls line up, and that pull is strongest when the Moon and Sun are at their nearest.
The name began in Australia in 2009 and is now used in places like South Florida, where these predictable tides can cause flooding.

facts.label: Time of year
facts.value: Near perihelion, when Earth is closest to the Sun in early January

items.prompt: Two full moons fall six months apart, one in early January and one in early July, with the Moon equally close both times. Which brings the higher tide?

options.label: The July one, because it is summer
Both bring exactly the same tide
The July one, because the Sun is farther
The January one, because Earth is nearer the Sun

items.explain: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, so the Sun's pull is stronger and tides are enhanced; in early July it is farthest and tides are reduced.

items.prompt: The Moon is at half phase, a week after the new moon. Is this a time when a king tide happens?

options.label: Yes, half moons bring the highest tides
No, they come at new and full moon
Yes, but only in the southern hemisphere
No, they only happen during storms

items.explain: King tides happen at new and full moon, when the Earth, Moon and Sun line up.

items.prompt: A city wants to warn residents about next year's king tides well in advance. Is that possible?

options.label: Yes, they are natural and predictable
No, they appear at random
Only a day or two ahead, like storms
No, they depend entirely on rainfall

items.explain: King tides are naturally occurring, predictable events driven by the positions of the Earth, Moon and Sun.

items.prompt: A full moon happens while the Moon is at the closest point of its orbit around Earth. What does that do to the tide?

options.label: Makes it smaller, since the pull evens out
Has no effect; only the Sun's distance matters
Makes it larger, since the pull is strongest
Delays it by about a week

items.explain: The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth is greatest at perigee, its closest point, which boosts the tidal range.

items.prompt: A king tide is forecast to reach a certain height, but on the day strong winds and rough seas hit the coast. What happens to the water level?

options.label: It stays exactly at the forecast
It can climb above the forecast
It always falls below the forecast
The king tide is cancelled entirely

items.explain: Local weather patterns and ocean conditions can push a king tide higher than its predicted height.

items.prompt: If you had to name the single biggest pull behind Earth's tides, what would it be?

options.label: The Sun
Ocean winds
Underwater earthquakes
The Moon

items.explain: The Moon has a larger effect on the tides than the Sun, though the Sun's position also matters.
